most_helpful.title: We've All Rolled The Dice on $30
most_helpful.body:
By word of mouth of these types of products, I began to look into them.  After reading many reviews they all seem mixed. Some good, some bad. I will say, as someone who wouldn't blink at dropping $30 on a bottle of whiskey every two weeks, why would I cringe spending that same money on something that might help me? Through this logic, I went ahead and ordered a bag of the mushroom coffee. It took a minute to show up but when it did, I took a big ol' scoop and plopped it in my coffee.  Expecting a bit of an earthy taste and a bit of grittiness, I was correct. It didn't bother me much. I kind of looked forward to it actually. But, it wasn't a couple hours that went by and I noticed I was actually getting things done. This was a big deal for me because of my A.D.D. (I know, we all can say we have it). I really do. Executive function has been a weakness of mine for years and I just jump to the next thing when my brain can't hang on any longer on the task. It takes extreme pressure and very negative consequences to motivate me to get something done and I've been that way for years.  But here I am, 2 hours after drinking this, I'm bubble gutting and focused. Everything I'm doing has resolve and that part of my brain that keeps me from finishing things plummets. What's weird, is that i wasn't even thinking about how I never finish anything while I was just doing it. So, in short, for me, this product is a must. Also, I dropped 8lbs in the first week. Be stocked up on t.p. is all I'm saying. But, that's a good thing. I eat like a trash panda so I wasn't surprised this happened. It helped suppressed appetite at first but I will say my body leveled out and my desire to continue being a garbage disposal ramped back up. But that's on me. 
I'd say to anyone else, whether it works through it's actual benefits or possibly through a placebo affect, does it matter? We spend so much more on things we already convince ourselves make us feel better. And to those that try it and it doesn't work, I'm pretty sure somewhere along the way in your life, you spent way more on things that didn't give you a return. My recommendation? Give it a shot.  We all spend money on research and development for ourselves on things that don't work out. But for $30-$40, I think this is well worth the roll of the dice.
